questions.def: 'But' shows contrast between wanting to go and the rain.
questions.question: I want to go to the park ___ it's raining.

questions.def: 'Therefore' shows cause and effect: study leads to passing.
questions.question: He studied hard; ___, he passed the exam.

questions.def: 'Because' introduces a reason for staying inside.
questions.question: We stayed inside ___ it was raining.

questions.def: 'While' contrasts her tea preference with my coffee.
questions.question: She likes tea, ___ I prefer coffee.

questions.def: 'Because' gives the reason for going to the shop.
questions.question: I went to the shop ___ I needed milk.

questions.def: 'Because' explains why he failed; 'studying' = gerund.
questions.question: He failed the test ___ not ___ enough.

questions.def: 'But' shows a contrast between wealth and happiness.
questions.question: He is rich, ___ he is not happy.

questions.def: 'Therefore' shows the result of not studying.
questions.question: She didn't study; ___, she failed.

questions.def: 'After' indicates sequence; 'eating' is correct verb form.
questions.question: I will go to the shop ___ I finish ___.

questions.def: 'And' joins two similar items: apples and bananas.
questions.question: I like apples ___ bananas.

questions.def: 'So' indicates consequence: tiredness leads to bed.
questions.question: She is tired, ___ she will go to bed.

questions.def: 'Because' gives the reason; 'worked' in past simple.
questions.question: He is tired ___ he ___ all day.

questions.def: 'But' shows contrast between desire and lack of money.
questions.question: She wants to travel ___ she has no money.

questions.def: 'When' indicates the time I will call.
questions.question: I will call you ___ I arrive.

questions.def: 'After' shows sequence; 'finish' in present simple.
questions.question: I will go home ___ I ___ my work.

questions.def: 'So' shows the consequence of not eating.
questions.question: He didn't eat, ___ he was hungry.

questions.def: 'And' joins two similar activities.
questions.question: I like to read books ___ watch movies.

questions.def: 'Until' shows the duration; 'arrive' in present simple.
questions.question: I will stay here ___ you ___.

questions.def: 'But' shows contrast: desire vs. high price.
questions.question: I wanted to buy it, ___ it was too expensive.

questions.def: 'Therefore' connects cause (good student) to effect (grades).
questions.question: He is a good student; ___, he gets good grades.

questions.def: Use 'Although' instead of 'Despite' when followed by a clause.
questions.question: Despite he was tired, he finished the work.

questions.def: 'After' shows sequence; 'cooks' in present simple.
questions.question: I will eat ___ she ___ dinner.

questions.def: 'Because' explains the reason for studying hard.
questions.question: She studies hard ___ she wants to pass.

questions.def: 'Because of' is followed by a noun phrase (traffic).
questions.question: He is late ___ the traffic.

questions.def: "But" shows contrast between wanting to go and the rain.
questions.question: I want to go to the park ___ it's raining.

questions.def: "In order to" indicates purpose or intention.
questions.question: She studied hard ___ pass the exam.

questions.def: "Additionally" is an adverb connecting ideas.
questions.question: ___ to the cost of the car, you need insurance.

questions.def: "So" indicates a result or consequence.
questions.question: He was tired, ___ he went to bed early.

questions.def: "Despite" introduces a contrast or something unexpected.
questions.question: ___ the rain, we enjoyed the picnic.

questions.def: "However" introduces a contrasting idea.
questions.question: It was a difficult test; ___, most students passed.
